text:
PANDIR

Dua tiga hari ni, sis dok baca hujah seorang EXCO Pertanian. Puncanya, dia nak pertahankan kenyataan Presidennya.

Hujahnya ada 2
 1. “Tiada minyak kita lalu Selat Hormuz”
 2. “Minyak kita pula dieksport ke Filipina”

Premis hujah dia sangat simplistik. 

Semua minyak mentah kita tak patut dijual kepada negara luar. Malaysia juga tak patut proses dan tapis minyak dan eksport ke luar negara. 

Kalau dia yang uruskan Petronas/ negara, solusinya: apa sahaja minyak mentah kita, yang kita jumpa kita proses, kita bagi kat orang kita. Nescaya cukup, dan harga takkan mahal.

Dengan kata lain, hentikan eksport minyak mentah kita. Hentikan import minyak dari negara luar. Sure isu minyak kita selesai.

Hujah ni, at the surface nampak macam hebat. Mak aiiii… senang sgt.

Tapi saya seriau menengokkan. Level fahaman EXCO Pertanian ini tentang industri oil and gas negara.

Kalau dia naik jadi Menteri, boleh melingkup Petronas dibuatnya. 

****************

Perkara pertama saya nak tanya: 

Adakah dia tahu minyak mentah Malaysia ni minyak premium? 

Light Sweet Oil Malaysia adalah antara yang paling dikehendaki dalam pasaran. Sebab minyak kita pure dari dasar laut. Senang nak diproses takde banyak sulfur. Harga dia USD4-5 lebih mahal dari Brent Crude.

Minyak kita diproses untuk kegunaan premium seperti minyak jet dan bahan plastik.

Sejak penubuhan Petronas tahun 70-an. Ini lah business model nya. Petronas jual harga tinggi minyak negara, dan import pula minyak negara luar yang lebih murah sesuai diguna untuk kereta. Itu yang datang untungnya.

Untuk rekod, 38% minyak import kita datang dari Selat Hormuz. 

Bayangkan kalau Petronas hanya gali dan proses minyak kita.

Bekal minyak yang patutnya untuk jet dan plastik, pi guna untuk kereta 🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️

Adakah itu solusi EXCO tersebut? 
Nescaya boleh meranap Petronas dibuatnya.

*****************

Solusi EXCO punya mudah. Semua minyak mentah kita, kita proses dan kita yang guna. Maka selesai cerita.

Tapi apa implikasi solusi ini?

Malaysia tak eksport dan import minyak. Petronas meranap. Negara terkesan. 

Solusi yang surface konon nampak bijak. 
Tapi hancus, bila micronya dia tak nampak.

***********

Saya tak faham macam mana Pembangkang bangkang isu minyak ni. 

Petrol kurang isu setakat ni. Rakyat Malaysia dapat harga RM1.99 seliter, antara yang terendah di dunia. Lagi murah dari Saudi. Nikmat mana yang nak didusta lagi?

Diesel pula ada sektor disubsidi. Ada yang tidak. Rakan2 kita pakai 4x4 dan Hilux banyak sangkut jua. Kereta pun takleh gerak. Diesel mahal punya angkara. 

Makanya, ini patutnya bullet yang Pembangkang guna. Desak Kerajaan lindungi mereka. Bagi solusi yang lebih baik. Tunjukkan kalau anda memerintah, kita boleh yakin anda boleh urus negara.

Ini bagi solusi merepek jauh dari realiti. 
Bila kita tegur berpusing-pusing.

Masalah besar bila ada EXCO kita fikir urus minyak negara macam masak Maggi. 
Jumpa, masak, makan, selesai.

Saya tak pasti ini strategi memandirkan pengundi. Atau dia yang pandir sendiri.

Salam hormat,
Liyana Marzuki

NB- sis kurang mahir tentang lembu dan padi. Tapi pasal trade minyak ni boleh lah bagi inputs serba sedikit. Pernah jadi Pegawai Khas di MITI ✌🏼

Malaysia dah jadi net importer minyak sejak 2014.
The Star sudah lapor pada 21 Jan 2015 lagi berdasarkan data kerajaan.
Jadi ini bukan isu baru.
Ini yang saya panggil shifting the goalpost - defensive statement style.

Soalan sebenar bukan bila kita jadi net importer.
Soalan sebenar apa yang dibuat oleh pihak bertanggungjawab sejak 2014?
Mana-
-Kementerian Ekonomi
-Kementerian Kewangan
-Kementerian Tenaga
-PETRONAS
-EPU
-National Economic Council

Apa pelan 10 tahun kita sebagai net importer?
-Strategic petroleum reserve?
-Tambah refining capacity?
-Fuel diversification?
-Kurangkan fuel dependency melalui pengangkutan awam?
-Renewable energy scale-up?

Atau kita hanya sedar risiko bila Middle East ada konflik?
Kalau setiap kali krisis global baru kita panik,
maknanya kita tidak merancang - kita hanya bertindak bila terdesak.
Harap-harap krisis Middle East yang berlaku hari ini
tidak hanya akan kita "faham" pada tahun 2030 nanti.
Ini bukan isu minyak.

KERAJAAN MADANI PERLUAS PERLINDUNGAN BIL ELEKTRIK KEPADA PENGGUNA DOMESTIK SEHINGGA 800 kWj
 
Kerajaan MADANI hari ini telah memutuskan untuk menambah baik subsidi bil elektrik untuk rakyat dengan memperluaskan tahap perlindungan daripada 600 kWj kepada 800 kWj sebulan berkuat kuasa bagi penggunaan elektrik mulai September hingga 31 Disember 2026. Langkah ini diambil sebagai tindakan segera bagi menangani tekanan hidup rakyat saat ini.
 
Melalui langkah ini, pengguna domestik yang menggunakan elektrik sehingga 800 kWj sebulan akan diberikan perlindungan melibatkan pengecualian Pelarasan Kos Bahan Api Automatik (AFA), Caj Peruncitan dan Cukai Jualan dan Perkhidmatan (Sales & Service Tax).
 
Sekalung penghargaan khususnya kepada pihak TNB, PETRA dan Suruhanjaya Tenaga atas peranan mereka dalam memungkinkan langkah ini diambil dalam kadar segera.
 
Keadaan jerebu serta cuaca yang lebih panas mutakhir ini telah mendorong peningkatan penggunaan elektrik dalam kalangan sebahagian isi rumah, menyebabkan penggunaan bulanan mereka melepasi paras 600 kWj dan menyebabkan kenaikan bil yang luar biasa.
 
Justeru itu, Kerajaan MADANI akan terus memantau rapi perkembangan kos bahan api dan keadaan pasaran tenaga semasa bagi memastikan sebarang keputusan berkaitan tarif elektrik mengambil kira keseimbangan antara kemampuan dan beban hidup rakyat, keterjaminan bekalan elektrik dan kemampanan sektor tenaga negara.

ANWAR IBRAHIM

Ringkasan Laporan Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) Mengenai Tabung Haji

Laporan ini meneliti pengurusan dan operasi Lembaga Tabung Haji (LTH) bagi tempoh 2014 hingga 2020. 

Laporan tersebut disediakan oleh Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja yang ditubuhkan oleh Kerajaan Malaysia untuk menyiasat isu berkaitan tadbir urus, pengurusan kewangan dan operasi Tabung Haji.

Suruhanjaya mendapati terdapat beberapa kelemahan besar dalam tadbir urus, termasuk:

* Kuasa menteri yang terlalu luas di bawah Akta Tabung Haji 1995. 🔥🔥

* Ketiadaan syarat kelayakan yang jelas bagi pelantikan Pengerusi dan ahli Lembaga Pengarah.

* Pengaruh politik dalam urusan pelantikan dan keputusan penting, termasuk pengagihan hibah serta subsidi haji.

* Konflik kepentingan apabila ahli Lembaga Pengarah turut memegang jawatan dalam beberapa syarikat subsidiari.

* Pemantauan yang lemah terhadap pelaburan, pelaporan kewangan dan pengurusan risiko.

Suruhanjaya mengesyorkan:

* Akta Tabung Haji 1995 dipinda bagi memperkukuh tadbir urus.

* Tanggungjawab pengawasan dikongsi antara Menteri yang bertanggungjawab terhadap Hal Ehwal Agama dan Menteri Kewangan.

* Kriteria pelantikan ahli Lembaga Pengarah diperjelaskan dengan memberi keutamaan kepada kepakaran dan pengalaman profesional.

* Pengaruh politik dikurangkan serta ketelusan, akauntabiliti dan tadbir urus kewangan diperkukuh.

* Pemantauan terhadap pelaburan ditambah baik bagi melindungi kepentingan para pendeposit.

Secara keseluruhannya, laporan tersebut menyimpulkan bahawa Tabung Haji memerlukan reformasi tadbir urus yang menyeluruh untuk memulihkan keyakinan masyarakat, memastikan pengurusan kewangan yang berhemat serta melindungi simpanan para pendeposit Islam di Malaysia.

1. Penolakan Terhadap "Birokrasi Dinasti"

Punchline yang sering dilaungkan oleh pembangkang mengenai "Parti Anak Beranak" akhirnya menjadi barah dalaman. Akar umbi dan pemimpin pertengahan melihat hierarki PKR tidak lagi menawarkan mobiliti kerjaya politik yang adil kepada mereka yang berada di luar faksi utama.

BERSAMA, di bawah Presiden Ahmad Syukri Che Abdul Razab dan Rafizi Ramli serta Nik Nazmi sebagai pemimpin de facto, menawarkan struktur baharu yang bersih daripada bayang-bayang nepotisme.

2. Magnet Ideologi "Sang Kancil" & Agenda Ekonomi

Menggunakan simbol Kancil berlatarbelakangkan bintang, BERSAMA memposisikan diri sebagai alternatif yang cerdik dan bersedia menumbangkan gergasi politik feudal.

Di kawasan Malay Belt, naratif mereka sangat tajam: menolak retorik perkauman sempit tetapi memberi fokus kepada isu poket rakyat melalui 12-point agenda (gaji adil, bantuan bulanan, kos sara hidup). Ini merupakan tawaran yang gagal diberikan oleh PKR yang kini terikat dengan kompromi sebuah Kerajaan Persekutuan yang besar.

3. Langkah Solo: Menolak Politik Gabungan

Satu tamparan hebat kepada landskap politik sedia ada ialah ketegasan BERSAMA untuk bergerak secara solo. Mereka enggan menjadi talian hayat kepada Pakatan Harapan mahupun Perikatan Nasional.

Strategi ini memikat pengundi atas pagar yang mengalami keletihan politik (political fatigue) akibat drama pusingan U gabungan-gabungan besar.

⚡ IMPAK SEGERA: "REMPUHAN" PERTAMA DI SELATAN

Langkah BERSAMA membuka permohonan calon secara terbuka di laman web mereka bukan sekadar gimik. Ia merupakan persediaan jentera perang untuk menghadapi dua ujian getir yang terdekat:

PRN Johor (11 Julai 2026)

PRN Negeri Sembilan (1 Ogos 2026)

Johor, terutamanya dengan spekulasi penyertaan tokoh tempatan pro-teknokrat yang tidak lagi bertanding di bawah bendera lama, bakal menjadi makmal ujian pertama. Sama ada "Sang Kancil" ini bakal memecahkan monopoli parti-parti tradisional atau memberi platform kepada pengundi atas pagar yang benci politik coalition.

Satu perkara yang pasti: empayar Keadilan yang dibina sejak 1999 kini secara rasmi berhadapan dengan cermin retaknya sendiri.

Sebagai langkah menangani kesan krisis bekalan tenaga dan bahan asas akibat Perang Timur Tengah awal tahun ini, Kerajaan Negeri Selangor memperkenalkan Pakej Pengukuhan Daya Tahan Selangor dengan nilai sejumlah RM140 juta sebagai penampan untuk membantu rakyat. Inisiatif ini memfokuskan kepada keterjaminan bekalan makanan, kawalan inflasi, dan bantuan langsung. 

Berikut adalah inisiatif utama di bawah pakej ini:

 ✅Baucar Kita Selangor: Bantuan bernilai RM100 sebulan (selama 6 bulan) diberikan kepada 50,000 penerima terpilih bagi meringankan beban kos kehidupan harian.

🚌Subsidi Pengangkutan: Bantuan subsidi pengangkutan awam/minyak bernilai RM30 sebulan. Permohonan dan penebusan telah dibuka bermula 1 Jun 2026 melalui aplikasi NINE. 

🥬Program Jualan Ehsan Rahmah (JER): Peningkatan peruntukan sebanyak RM5 juta untuk menawarkan barangan asas pada harga murah untuk kesejahteraan perbelanjaan warga Selangor.

🥣Inisiatif Sarapan Percuma: memanfaatkan pelajar di 965 sekolah di seluruh negeri. Program yang diuruskan melalui 12 Pihak Berkuasa Tempatan (PBT) ini bertujuan untuk meringankan perbelanjaan ibu bapa dan memastikan murid mendapat nutrisi yang baik sebelum memulakan sesi pembelajaran. 

👨🏻‍🌾Bantuan Sektor Pertanian: Peruntukan sebanyak RM25 juta disalurkan untuk membantu lebih 14,000 pengusaha agromakanan bagi menangani peningkatan kos operasi dan memastikan keterjaminan bekalan makanan. 

Pelaksanaan bantuan ini bermula 15 Jun 2026 sebagai fasa pertama, manakala fasa kedua pula sedang dirangka bagi menyokong kelangsungan sektor perindustrian negeri.

Konvensyen PH umpama paluan 'gendang perang' - Fahmi Fadzil 

1. Saya baca kenyataan saudara Fahmi Fadzil. Dia kata Konvensyen Pakatan Harapan (PH) 2026 di Johor ini seumpama paluan gendang perang.

2. Saya bersetuju. Memang sudah tiba masanya gendang dipalu. Kalau diam sahaja, musuh akan ingat kita lemah.

3. Tiga tahun pertama pemerintahan, Kerajaan PH sibuk membersihkan kerosakan lama. Baiki sistem subsidi, laksanakan penyasaran RON95 dan diesel. Dasar-dasar ini dibetulkan supaya negara tidak muflis.

4. Ini kerja yang susah dan tidak popular. Ramai yang marah. Tetapi untuk selamatkan masa depan kewangan negara, ia mesti dibuat. Pemimpin PH berani ambil risiko ini kerana mereka ikhlas mahu pulihkan negara, bukan sekadar cari undi.

5. Sekarang, selepas ekonomi mula stabil, tumpuan kena diberi semula kepada gerak kerja parti. PRN Johor dan Melaka mungkin akan diadakan. Pilihan Raya Umum juga kita tidak tahu bila. Kita mesti sedia dari awal.

6. Arahan Perdana Menteri supaya menteri-menteri PH fokus selesaikan masalah rakyat yang tertangguh adalah mesej yang sangat tepat. Rakyat, terutamanya penjaja, peniaga kecil dan golongan susah mesti dibela.

7. Rakyat menilai kerajaan dari apa yang mereka rasa di bawah. Kalau pemimpin sibuk di pejabat dan leka, rakyat akan lari.

8. Pembahagian kerusi antara PKR, AMANAH dan DAP mesti mula dirunding dengan baik-baik. Jangan tamak. Kalau kita bergaduh sesama sendiri rebut kerusi, musuh akan menang mudah. Kita sudah lihat benda ini terjadi banyak kali.

9. Konvensyen ini penting untuk merapatkan semula saf dan menyatukan jentera ketiga-tiga parti. Jentera kena rajin turun padang terangkan kepada rakyat apa kejayaan dan pembaharuan yang Kerajaan dah capai.

10. Jika PH kekal berpegang pada prinsip tolak rasuah dan berkerja keras bela nasib orang biasa, saya yakin rakyat yang waras akan terus beri sokongan. 

11. Gendang perang sudah berbunyi, sekarang masa untuk turun padang dan pastikan kemenangan.

"Bagitau masalah yang semua orang dah tau, mana solution?"

I don't think semua orang dah tau. At best, orang tau harga minyak naik sejak perang bermula. Tapi ramai taktau shortages barang-barang lain yang dah mula menggigit sektor perkilangan dan pembuatan. 

Mana solution? 

Krisis dan kejutan bekalan tenaga sekarang, unprecedented dan paling buruk dalam sejarah dunia. Sama macam Covid, Kerajaan takde penyelesaian selain mengikut apa yang dunia buat iaitu lockdown. 

Masa Covid Kerajaan boleh bantu rakyat, buat stimulus package, tambah perbelanjaan, bagi rakyat duit. 

Bezanya hari ini kita berdepan dengan masalah bekalan. Bukan sekadar minyak tapi produk lain yang kita guna setiap hari. 

Tambah duit atau perbelanjaan tidak akan menyelesaikan masalah bekalan. Bekalan yang terputus kerana Selat Hormuz disekat tidak akan selesai dengan menambah perbelanjaan Kerajaan. 

Tapi Kerajaan tetap bantu pesawah dan MSME untuk kurangkan beban kenaikan kos.

Apa kita boleh buat? Kawal perbelanjaan dan penggunaan untuk kekalkan kertersediaan/availability of supply selama yang mungkin. 

Kenapa Kerajaan potong perbelanjaan mengurus (OE)? Sebab undang-undang tak membenarkan Kerajaan meminjam untuk membiayai OE. Perbelanjaan subsidi minyak meningkat, perbelanjaan lain terpaksa dikurangkan untuk pastikan hasil cukup untuk membiayai OE. 

Solusi sekarang sesuai secara bersasar bukan secara pukal.

text:
Subsidi RON95 Mungkin Dipotong Lagi Kepada 150 Liter Sebulan

OLEH MYNEWSHUB 

KUALA LUMPUR – Kerajaan sedang mempertimbangkan untuk mengurangkan lagi had subsidi petrol RON95 di bawah program BUDI95 daripada 200 liter kepada 150 liter sebulan, dalam usaha memperkemas pengurusan subsidi dan mengurangkan ketirisan.

Timbalan Menteri Kewangan, Liew Chin Tong berkata, cadangan itu dibuat berdasarkan data penggunaan rakyat yang menunjukkan majoriti pengguna sebenarnya menggunakan petrol jauh lebih rendah daripada had semasa.

Menurut beliau, sebelum ini kuota subsidi telah dikurangkan daripada 300 liter kepada 200 liter pada Mac lalu sebagai fasa awal rasionalisasi subsidi bahan api.

“Data secara konsisten menunjukkan 80 peratus rakyat Malaysia menggunakan kurang daripada 200 liter sebulan. Langkah seterusnya ialah 150 liter kerana kira-kira 60 peratus populasi menggunakan kurang daripada 150 liter,” katanya ketika sesi fireside chat pada program Affin Market Outlook 2026 pada Selasa.

Beliau turut menjelaskan bahawa langkah itu bukan sekadar pengurangan subsidi, sebaliknya sebahagian daripada strategi pengurusan permintaan bahan api bagi memastikan bekalan domestik negara kekal stabil sekiranya konflik geopolitik dunia berpanjangan.

Dalam masa sama, kerajaan juga dilaporkan sedang mengkaji langkah mengetatkan kelayakan subsidi dengan kemungkinan mengecualikan golongan berpendapatan tinggi (T20) serta warga asing daripada menikmati subsidi RON95.

Bagaimanapun, Liew menegaskan kerajaan masih mahu memastikan golongan rentan termasuk penunggang motosikal dan isi rumah berpendapatan rendah terus menikmati akses kepada bahan api bersubsidi.

“Secara politik, saya mahu memastikan penunggang motosikal terus menikmati kadar subsidi tinggi. Mereka hanya menggunakan sekitar 50 liter sebulan dan golongan ini paling terkesan jika harga meningkat,” katanya.

Selain itu, kerajaan turut merancang mekanisme subsidi diesel bersasar untuk Sabah dan Sarawak, selain menggalakkan pelaburan lebih besar dalam pengangkutan awam serta penggunaan kenderaan elektrik bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan negara terhadap minyak dalam jangka panjang. - MYNEWSHUB

Langkah seterusnya ialah 150 liter kerana kira-kira 60 peratus populasi menggunakan kurang daripada 150 liter,” katanya ketika sesi fireside chat pada program Affin Market Outlook 2026 pada Selasa. Berucap dalam Perhimpunan Bulanan Kementerian Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam, beliau menekankan bahawa setiap dasar perlu digarap berteraskan nilai keadilan dan keseimbangan, selaras dengan konsep ummatan wasatan — yang menuntut keharmonian antara pertumbuhan ekonomi, kesejahteraan rakyat dan pemeliharaan alam sekitar.

Mengulas cabaran semasa, beliau menjelaskan bahawa ketidaktentuan geopolitik global serta konflik antarabangsa memberi tekanan kepada rantaian bekalan, kos tenaga dan harga barangan. Justeru, pendekatan fiskal yang lebih berhemah, strategik dan bersasar amat diperlukan bagi memastikan kestabilan ekonomi negara terus terpelihara.

Sehubungan itu, Kerajaan komited memperkukuh pelaksanaan penyasaran semula subsidi serta meningkatkan kecekapan penguatkuasaan bagi membendung ketirisan, sekali gus memastikan bantuan sampai kepada golongan yang benar-benar memerlukan.

Mengakhiri ucapan, Perdana Menteri menegaskan bahawa kejayaan agenda reformasi negara bergantung kepada integriti penjawat awam, kecekapan penyampaian serta kesepaduan seluruh jentera pentadbiran dalam melaksanakan amanah demi kesejahteraan rakyat dan kemakmuran negara.

SEMENCHU, 5 April 2026 – YAB Dato’ Seri Anwar bin Ibrahim, Perdana Menteri menegaskan komitmen kerajaan untuk memastikan FELDA terus diperkasa sebagai sebahagian daripada arus utama pembangunan negara. Semua inisiatif melibatkan pendidikan, TVET, belia, sukan dan keagamaan kini dilaksanakan secara menyeluruh agar manfaatnya dapat dirasai secara langsung oleh warga peneroka.

Beliau memaklumkan bahawa Kerajaan turut memikul tanggungjawab besar dalam menyelesaikan beban hutang lama FELDA dengan bayaran mencecah RM1 bilion, di samping memperkukuh aspek tadbir urus dan pengurusan. Dalam masa sama, keutamaan diberikan kepada penambahbaikan kemudahan asas termasuk cadangan penyediaan pusat dialisis di setiap kawasan bagi memudahkan akses rawatan kepada masyarakat.

Dalam ucapannya, beliau turut mengingatkan bahawa perkembangan geopolitik global memberi kesan langsung kepada ekonomi negara. Walaupun berdepan tekanan kos termasuk kenaikan harga baja dan bahan api, Malaysia masih mampu mengekalkan harga RON95 antara yang terendah di dunia, dengan Kerajaan menanggung hampir RM6 bilion sebulan bagi subsidi dan bantuan kepada rakyat.

Mengakhiri ucapan, beliau menyeru rakyat agar terus bersyukur, berjimat dan menolak sikap perpecahan, di samping mengekalkan keprihatinan terhadap isu kemanusiaan termasuk di Gaza. Sebagai tanda penghargaan kepada warga Semenchu, Kerajaan turut meluluskan peruntukan khas sebanyak RM500,000 bagi menaik taraf kemudahan asas setempat demi kesejahteraan komuniti FELDA.

Pagi ini saya berkunjung ke Kuala Kangsar untuk bertemu guru, anak-anak serta bekas pelajar Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Clifford. Di sebalik tekanan cabaran ekonomi akibat krisis tenaga global ketika ini, saya tegaskan bahawa soal pendidikan dan naik taraf kemudahan sekolah tetap menjadi keutamaan Kerajaan MADANI.

Dalam lawatan ini, saya tekankan bahawa projek kecil yang menyentuh keperluan harian pelajar, termasuk pembaikan kemudahan asas, mesti disegerakan tanpa berlengah. Keutamaan ini tidak boleh dikompromi walau dalam keadaan krisis, kerana masa depan anak-anak tidak boleh menjadi korban.

Namun dalam memastikan keutamaan ini terus dilaksana, kita tidak dapat lari daripada realiti bahawa dunia sedang berdepan krisis tenaga global yang kian meruncing, susulan konflik di Asia Barat yang menjejaskan bekalan minyak dan gas serta mencetuskan ketidaktentuan pasaran di seluruh dunia.

Tempiasnya turut dirasai di negara kita. Dalam keadaan ini, Kerajaan MADANI terus berikhtiar sedaya upaya memastikan rakyat tidak terbeban, termasuk mengekalkan harga RON95 pada kadar yang rendah serta meneruskan subsidi diesel kepada golongan yang memerlukan, sambil mengimbangi keperluan melindungi rakyat dan menjamin bekalan tenaga negara untuk jangka panjang.

Saya juga mengambil kesempatan untuk mengingatkan bahawa pendidikan kita perlu mengutamakan keupayaan berfikir secara kritis, memupuk nilai serta akhlak, di samping menguasai pelbagai bidang ilmu. Dalam dunia yang penuh cabaran ini, ilmu tanpa nilai boleh memesongkan arah jika tidak dipandu oleh adab dan keinsanan.

Dalam kesempatan sama, saya turut mengumumkan kelulusan peruntukan RM296,000 bagi kerja-kerja baik pulih bangunan hospital pertama di Kuala Kangsar yang kini digunakan oleh SMK Clifford, sebagai usaha memelihara warisan sejarah serta memastikan kemudahan pembelajaran yang lebih selesa dan kondusif kepada warga sekolah.

Insya-Allah, dengan keutamaan yang jelas terhadap pendidikan serta kefahaman dan kebersamaan dalam mendepani cabaran global, kita mampu mengharungi ujian ini bersama-sama, sambil terus membina masa depan negara yang lebih adil, berdaya tahan dan berteraskan nilai.

TAKLIMAT KRISIS TENAGA GLOBAL, 2 APRIL 2026:

1. Kesan Krisis Global: Malaysia terkesan dengan krisis tenaga global dan konflik Asia Barat yang mengganggu rantaian bekalan dunia serta menaikkan harga tenaga.

2. Jaminan Bekalan Petroleum: Bekalan petroleum negara dipastikan kekal mencukupi dan stabil melalui pemantauan harian oleh kerajaan, Petronas, dan pemain industri.

3. Pelan Kontingensi: Kerajaan telah menyediakan pelan untuk mendapatkan bekalan daripada pasaran alternatif jika berlaku gangguan berpanjangan.

4. Libat Urus Industri: Sesi libat urus berterusan diadakan bersama pemegang taruh untuk mendapatkan maklum balas masa nyata (real-time) dan menyelaraskan tindakan pantas.

5. Pengekalan Harga RON95: Harga petrol RON95 bersubsidi dikekalkan pada paras RM 1.99 seliter bagi mengurangkan beban rakyat.

6. Kawalan Bahan Api Tidak Bersubsidi: Penyelarasan harga bagi bahan api tidak bersubsidi dilakukan secara terkawal dan berperingkat.

7. Subsidi Diesel Diteruskan (SKDS): Perlindungan harga diteruskan untuk sektor logistik (RM 2.05/liter) dan pengangkutan awam serta darat barangan (RM 2.15/liter).

8. Bantuan Budi MADANI: Bantuan tunai sebanyak RM 300 sebulan serta kuota khas dan subsidi diesel diteruskan untuk pemandu yang layak, e-hailing, nelayan, dan sektor agromakanan.

9. Bekerja Dari Rumah (BDR): Dilaksanakan secara berperingkat untuk sektor awam bermula 15 April bagi mengurangkan penggunaan tenaga dan kesesakan trafik.

10. Kawalan Suhu Bangunan Kerajaan: Suhu penghawa dingin di bangunan-bangunan kerajaan ditetapkan pada tahap minimum 24 darjah Celsius.

11. Etika Pakaian Fleksibel: Penjawat awam digalakkan memakai pakaian yang sesuai dengan iklim tempatan (seperti batik atau kemeja korporat) untuk mengurangkan penggunaan penghawa dingin.

12. Komunikasi Telus: Kerajaan akan memberikan kemas kini secara berkala dan mengingatkan rakyat agar tidak menyebarkan maklumat palsu.

13. Seruan Berjimat-Cermat: Rakyat dan komuniti perniagaan diseru untuk berganding bahu mengelakkan pembaziran dan menggunakan tenaga secara berhemah.

JOHOR BAHRU – Kerajaan Negeri Johor kini sedang memperincikan pelbagai langkah strategik bagi mengurangkan tekanan kos sara hidup rakyat, susulan ketidaktentuan ekonomi global akibat konflik geopolitik dan ketegangan di Timur Tengah.

Langkah itu dibuat selaras dengan titah Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Pemangku Sultan Johor, yang sentiasa menekankan kepentingan menjaga kebajikan dan kesejahteraan rakyat di negeri itu.

Menurut kenyataan, kerajaan negeri bersama barisan EXCO sedang meneliti pendekatan bersasar bagi memastikan bantuan yang dirangka benar-benar memberi impak kepada rakyat, khususnya golongan yang terkesan dengan peningkatan kos sara hidup.

“Beberapa inisiatif komprehensif dan berimpak tinggi sedang diperhalusi dan dijangka diumumkan dalam masa terdekat,” menurut kenyataan itu.

Kenyataan berkenaan dimuat naik di media sosial milik Menteri Besar, Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.

Kerajaan Negeri turut menegaskan komitmen untuk melaksanakan setiap perancangan dengan teliti bagi memastikan kesejahteraan rakyat terus terpelihara, di samping merangsang pertumbuhan ekonomi Johor secara seimbang dan mampan.

Langkah proaktif ini dilihat penting dalam memastikan negeri itu kekal stabil dari segi ekonomi dan sosial, terutama dalam menghadapi cabaran global yang semakin mencabar ketika ini.

Keprihatinan baginda Tunku Mahkota Ismail dijangka akan memastikan rakyat Johor tidak terlalu terjejas andai situasi di Timur Tengah semakin buruk. –MYNEWSHUB

Penurunan Had BUDI95 Sementara, Langkah Awal Lindungi Rakyat – Adam Adli

oleh Mynewshub 

KUALA LUMPUR – Keputusan kerajaan menurunkan had penggunaan BUDI95 daripada 300 liter kepada 200 liter disifatkan sebagai langkah sementara yang diambil secara berhati-hati susulan ketegangan global, khususnya di Asia Barat.

Pengarah Komunikasi Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR), Adam Adli berkata, keputusan itu bukan dibuat secara tergesa-gesa, sebaliknya berdasarkan pertimbangan rapi terhadap situasi semasa yang memberi tekanan kepada bekalan minyak, gas serta kos sara hidup di peringkat global.

Menurut beliau, konflik yang semakin meruncing di rantau Asia Barat memberi kesan langsung kepada kestabilan bekalan dan harga komoditi utama dunia, sekali gus memerlukan kerajaan bertindak lebih awal bagi mengelakkan kesan lebih buruk kepada rakyat.

“Keputusan ini dibuat berdasarkan data sebenar penggunaan BUDI95 sejak diperkenalkan, yang menunjukkan purata penggunaan sekitar 100 liter sebulan dan majoriti besar rakyat menggunakan kurang daripada 200 liter,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Tambahnya, kerajaan memilih pendekatan lebih berhemat dengan menyesuaikan had penggunaan tanpa menaikkan harga BUDI95 yang kekal pada kadar RM1.99 seliter, sekali gus mengurangkan tekanan ke atas rakyat.

Dalam masa sama, beliau menjelaskan keperluan golongan tertentu terus diberi perhatian apabila pemandu e-hailing dan pekerja gig masih menikmati had sehingga 800 liter, manakala Sabah dan Sarawak kekal dengan diesel subsidi pada harga RM2.15 seliter dengan kawalan lebih ketat.

Beliau turut menegaskan bahawa subsidi merupakan hak rakyat dan tidak sepatutnya disalah guna oleh pihak tidak bertanggungjawab, justeru penguatkuasaan perlu diperkasakan dengan kerjasama orang ramai.

Selain itu, kerajaan juga terus memainkan peranan aktif di peringkat antarabangsa dalam menangani konflik Asia Barat, termasuk usaha diplomasi yang digerakkan oleh Anwar Ibrahim bagi memastikan kepentingan negara terus terpelihara.

Sehubungan itu, beliau menggesa semua pihak melihat langkah berkenaan dalam konteks lebih luas sebagai usaha kerajaan bertindak secara telus, bertanggungjawab dan proaktif demi menjamin kestabilan negara serta melindungi rakyat daripada kesan krisis global yang berpanjangan. – MYNEWSHUB

Dalam keadaan krisis sebegini, inisiatif BDR akan dapat mengurangkan penggunaan minyak bagi memastikan bekalan minyak bertahan lebih lama, serta para pekerja dapat mengurangkan kos sara hidup memandangkan harga barangan yang dijangka akan meningkat.

Mengapa Kerajaan mengambil masa begitu lama untuk melaksanakan inisiatif BDR ini? Mohon pihak Kerajaan segera memberikan arahan dan perincian mengenai perkara ini agar penjawat awam lebih jelas dengan keputusan yang telah diumumkan oleh Kerajaan, dan syarikat swasta turut digalakkan mengambil inisiatif yang sama.

text:
MENILAI SEORANG PM 

Dah masuk separuh penggal, honeymoon is over. Golongan Atas Pagar (GAP) yang dulu syok dengan DSAI mula-mula naik jadi PMX, sekarang dah mula tarik muka. Ada yang dah mula kritik dan menjauhi. 

Tapi itu standard sekali. Dah berapa cycle dah kita ada Perdana Menteri? 

Dari Pak Lah, DS Najib ke Tun M. 
Dari TS Muhy ke DS Ismail Sabri. 
Sama patternnya. Mula2 harapan kita tinggi, ini PM hopefully lain dari yang lain. Kena 1/2 tahun, popularity mereka menurun. 

Ingat bila kita syok dengan penggal pertama DS Najib. Dengan ETP dan 1 Malaysia. 
Tak berapa lama 1MDB meletup sudah. 
Habis lepas tu dark side dia keluar. 
Sampai meranap BN 60 tahun memerintah. 

Ingat pulak macam mana orang syok dengan Abah. Boleh baca doa. Masuk tahun kedua, dia sakit cerry berry pun orang buat bahan lawak. Orang dah start menyampah. 

Hatta Negarawan Ulung tak berkecuali. Masa jadi PM teruk juga kena troll dan dimaki. 

**************

Cuma Anwar Ibrahim ni sedikit lain. Orang benci dan caci dia level yang tak pernah kita lihat. Tiada PM yang dihentam dari banyak side. 

Asbab bila jadi Pembangkang 30 tahun lamanya. Keluar masuk penjara. Menjadi sasaran majoriti jentera Kerajaan lama. 

Dijadikan boogeyman. Kononnya Boneka US and IMF. Tali barut Israel. Ini semua propaganda yang melekat hingga kini. Makanya apa saja yang dibuat untuk negara, dipandang dari “lensa benci”. 

Sebagai penjawat awam dari tahun awal 2000, saya turut termakan dengan naratif ini. Saya cautious bila dia naik jadi Perdana Menteri. 

Ada benda kita puji. Contoh political stability, pengurusan subsidi dan kebolehan geopolitik. Ini kita patut bagi kredit. 

Tapi ada juga benda kita tak puas hati. Seperti rekod sembang tak serupa bikin. Tindakan korupsi dendam dan terpilih. Kita harapkan dia lain dari yang lain. 

Penyokong nya kata his hands are tied. Dia kena manage Kerajaan Perpaduan. Banyak kena kompromi. Pembenci dia nak dia turun kalau boleh semalam. Tak tertahan mereka lihat dia memerintah Malaysia. 

Pada saya, dia seorang PM yang mula2 masuk memerintah pun ramai dah benci. Hasil politik kebencian 30 tahun lamanya. 

Dia kena kerja kuat untuk tunjuk dia PM Malaysia, banyak side yang dia kena ambil hati. 

Selepas 3 tahun, ramai yang dah mula start tak puas hati. Termasuk penyokong sendiri. Tetapi itu standard mana2 Perdana Menteri. Takdenya GAP akan syok dengan satu-satu PM sepanjang masa. Ada ketika akan menyampah punya. 

Cuma bila tiba pilihanraya. Kita akan mula nilai prestasi. Merit dan demerit. Dan pilih the lesser evil pada negara. Dan sama ada belah lagi satu, bagi alternatif yang lebih baik pula. 

Yang paling penting, kita menilai bukan dari lensa benci. Atau berlandaskan persepsi. 
Tapi atas data dan fakta serta pencapaian sebenar. 

Kerana dalam pilihanraya, 
kita bukan sekadar memilih pemimpin, 
kitalah yang menentukan masa depan negara. 

Gagal seorang Perdana Menteri, 
yang turut gagal adalah kita. 

Moga Tuhan terus lindungi Malaysia dari pemimpin dan parti yang menjahanamkan negara. 

Dan kita tak tertutup mata untuk menilai mereka. 

Salam hormat,
Liyana Marzuki

text:
MINYAK: HARGA, SUBSIDI DAN KEJUTAN 

1. Siapa yang pernah mengikuti Sekolah Merdeka yang saya anjurkan melalui Institute for Leadership and Development Studies (LEAD) sejak 2014 pasti biasa dengan topik i. Harga dan ii. Subsidi dalam tema Politik-Ekonomi. 

2. Harga ditentukan oleh pasaran - permintaan dan penawaran. Dulu pensyarah saya ajar "Amin, jika kamu faham ini, kamu telah faham separuh daripada persoalan ekonomi." 

3. Bagaimanapun, harga boleh dipengaruhi oleh faktor-faktor lain termasuk antaranya cukai dan subsidi. Itu belum dikira faktor lain seperti monopoli, pencatutan, penipuan, perang, sekatan ekonomi dan sebagainya. 

4. Apabila harga minyak di pasaran berjumlah RM5 seliter misalnya, tetapi kita hanya membayar RM3 seliter, itu bukan bermaksud harga minyak adalah RM3 seliter. Harganya tetap RM5 seliter. Cuma, RM2 seliter dibayar oleh pihak lain. Pihak lain ini ialah syarikat dan individu yang membayar cukai. Ya, syarikat yang kamu mungkin tuduh sebagai kapitalis atau individu yang kamu kata kaya itu. Cuma kita tak boleh tentukan secara khusus syarikat atau individu mana bagi setiap liter yang disubsidi. 

Kita hanya membayar RM3. Selebihnya syarikat minyak berkaitan akan membuat proses tuntutan daripada kerajaan untuk setiap baki RM2 subsidi tersebut. 

Percaya atau tidak, jika ditanya syarikat dan individu yang membayar cukai ini, mereka hampir pasti lebih suka wang cukai mereka digunakan untuk beri lebih kepada sekolah, hospital, rumah ibadat dan sebagainya berbanding memberi subsidi minyak kepada kita. Jadi, eloklah kita berterima kasih kepada semua pembayar cukai kerana tanpa mereka, kerajaan sukar untuk membiayai subsidi. 

5. Ramai mengungkit cerita hampir 20 tahun lalu kerana Anwar Ibrahim bercakap tentang minyak boleh lebih murah ketika itu. Setuju atau tidak, dalam debat harga minyak, Anwar menunjukkan kepada kita tentang RM5 billion yang diperlukan bagi mengurangkan harga minyak ketika itu. 

Berapa harga minyak ketika itu? 
Harga minyak MOPS (Mean of Platts Singapore) pada tahun 2008 mencapai paras tertinggi dalam sejarah sebelum jatuh mendadak, selari dengan lonjakan harga minyak mentah dunia, berikutan krisis ekonomi global. Purata harga minyak mentah Asia-Pasifik (Tapis) adalah sekitar USD 103.69 setong, dengan harga runcit petrol di Malaysia naik sebanyak 78 sen - dari RM1.92 sekarang kepada RM2.70. Harga minyak diesel pula naik kepada RM2.58 - naik RM1 berbanding harga sekarang sebanyak RM1.58 seliter.

Kenaikan harga itu adalah sebahagian daripada langkah kerajaan untuk mengawal subsidi bagi menampung kenaikan petrol, diesel dan gas, yang dijangka berjumlah RM56 bilion pada tahun tersebut. Kerajaan mahu menjimatkan RM4 bilion di bawah penstrukturan semula skim subsidi tersebut.

Tanpa subsidi, harga pada masa itu sebenarnya dianggarkan sekitar RM3.30-RM3.80 bagi petrol dan RM3.00-RM3.50 bagi diesel. 

Logiknya, anggaran RM5 billion Anwar pada ketika itu munasabah kerana kerajaan sendiri mengumumkan pelarasan harga dibuat bagi menjimatkan RM4 billion. Sama ada kita bersetuju dengan cadangan Anwar pada ketika itu, termasuk dari mana sumber RM5 billion itu dicadangkan diambil adalah soal kedua, dan menjadi akademik. 

Untuk rekod, bagi tahun 2007, cukai pendapatan petroleum kerajaan ialah RM20.5 billion, dividen Petronas RM24.0 billion, royalti petroleum RM4.2 billion. Bagi tahun 2008, cukai pendapatan petroleum berjumlah RM24.1 billion, dividen Petronas RM30.0 billion dan royalti petroleum RM6.2 billion. Cukai pendapatan petroleum bagi tahun 2009 pula ialah RM27.2 billion, dividen RM30.0 billion dan royalti petroleum RM6.6 billion. 

Saya hanya menunjukkan angka-angka daripada Laporan Ekonomi 2007-2009 sesuai dengan kadar terdekat isu yang dibincang. 

Angka-angka ini mungkin boleh dipersoalkan lagi kerana laporan berasaskan tahun kewangan Petronas menunjukkan bayaran kepada kerajaan ialah RM52.3 billion (2007), RM67.6 billion (2008), dan RM74.0 billion (2009)

Subsidi BUDI95 Diturunkan Kepada 200 Liter, Rakyat Hanya Guna 100 Liter - PM Anwar 

Oleh Mynewshub

KUALA LUMPUR - Kerajaan akan menurunkan kelayakan penggunaan BUDI95 daripada 300 liter kepada hanya 200 liter sebulan berkuat kuasa 1 April ini.

Perdana Menteri, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim berkata, langkah itu merupakan pendekatan bersasar bagi memastikan subsidi bahan api terus dinikmati majoriti rakyat.

"Kita meneliti apakah penggunaan BUDI95 ini mencukupi. Kita dapati, purata penggunaan BUDI95 adalah sekitar 100 liter.

"Maknanya majoriti rakyat guna hanya 100 liter sebulan dan hampir 90 peratus rakyat menggunakan kurang dari 200 liter sebulan, maka tidak terjejas," katanya.

Beliau berkata demikian semasa menyampaikan perutusan khas berhubung langkah strategik negara dalam memperkukuh kesiapsiagaan mendepani krisis tenaga global susulan konflik di Asia Barat.

Anwar berkata, langkah itu bersifat sementara menunggu keadaan minyak, bekalan minyak dan ekonomi dunia pulih walau belum ada tanda-tanda ke arah itu. - MYNEWSHUB

text:
Ada media yang tidak jelas sumbernya menyatakan bahawa:

“Kerajaan dijangka mengurangkan kuota subsidi petrol RON95 di bawah BUDI95 daripada 300 kepada 200 liter sebulan bermula April.”

Setakat ini, tidak dapat dipastikan dari mana sumber maklumat tersebut diperoleh.

Dalam situasi geopolitik dunia yang tidak menentu ketika ini, khususnya susulan konflik di Asia Barat yang menjejaskan rantaian bekalan minyak global, banyak negara telah berdepan kenaikan harga bahan api yang mendadak. Ada negara terpaksa menutup stesen petrol kerana bekalan minyak habis, manakala ada juga yang menghadkan jumlah penjualan minyak setiap hari. Malah, rakyat di beberapa negara terpaksa membeli petrol pada harga jauh lebih tinggi tanpa sebarang subsidi daripada kerajaan.

Jika benar kuota subsidi diselaraskan kepada 200 liter sebulan, langkah itu masih menunjukkan komitmen kerajaan untuk terus melindungi rakyat daripada kesan penuh kenaikan harga minyak dunia. Dengan harga RON95 kekal sekitar RM1.99 seliter bagi kuota yang ditetapkan, rakyat Malaysia masih menikmati antara harga petrol paling rendah di rantau ini.

Kajian juga menunjukkan bahawa 90% pengguna BUDI95 menggunakan kurang daripada 200 liter sebulan. Ini bermakna, jika angka 200 liter itu benar-benar dikuatkuasakan kelak, 90% rakyat tidak akan terjejas langsung.

Pendekatan ini juga selari dengan usaha kerajaan untuk memastikan subsidi dilaksanakan secara lebih bersasar, supaya manfaatnya benar-benar dinikmati oleh golongan yang memerlukan, tanpa membebankan kedudukan fiskal negara.

Dalam keadaan ekonomi global yang mencabar hari ini, mengekalkan harga RON95 pada RM1.99 walaupun dengan pelarasan kuota boleh dilihat sebagai satu keseimbangan antara menjaga kebajikan rakyat dan memastikan kewangan negara kekal mampan.

Bangkok Post melaporkan Menteri Kewangan Thailand, Ekniti Nitithanprapas mengumumkan bahawa mereka akan berhenti memberi subsidi minyak secara pukal dan sebaliknya membuat subsidi bersasar kepada sektor yang terjejas paling teruk dari konflik Perang US Iran ini

Harga minyak kini akan ikut pasaran dengan subsidi pukal telah menyebabkan Kerajaan Thailand kehilangan bajet yang tidak perlu. Thailand mengumumkan mengurangkan cukai Eksais bagi mengurangkan kenaikan harga minyak

Sebelum ini Kerajaan Thailand terpaksa membelanjakan RM 2.4 Bilion dalam masa 3 minggu dengan kos RM 120 Juta sehari. Namun harga minyak yang naik menyebabkan Thailand terpaksa belanja RM 300 Juta sehari. 

Harga Minyak Diesel juga naik kepada RM 3.28 seliter dan RM 1.18 seliter untuk petrol. Sebelum ini Thailand berjanji tidak akan benarkan Harga Diesel melebihi RM 4 seliter. Bill elektrik Thailand dijangka naik 18 peratus susulan pengakhiran subsidi ini

Menurut kenyataan Kementerian Kewangan Malaysia (MOF), kenaikan itu didorong oleh konflik berpanjangan di Asia Barat sejak penghujung Februari lalu yang menyebabkan lonjakan harga minyak mentah global.

Bagi tempoh tersebut, harga baharu yang ditetapkan adalah seperti berikut:

RON97 naik kepada RM5.15 seliter

RON95 tanpa subsidi meningkat kepada RM3.87 seliter

RON95 bersubsidi (BUDI95) kekal RM1.99 seliter

Diesel di Semenanjung Malaysia naik kepada RM5.52 seliter

Diesel di Sabah, Sarawak dan Labuan kekal RM2.15 seliter

Kenaikan ini menunjukkan lonjakan berbanding minggu sebelumnya (19 hingga 25 Mac 2026), di mana RON97 berada pada RM4.55 seliter dan diesel Semenanjung pada RM4.72 seliter.

Kerajaan memaklumkan bahawa pelarasan dibuat secara berperingkat bagi mengimbangi kesan kenaikan harga global, sambil mengekalkan subsidi bagi RON95 untuk melindungi majoriti rakyat.

Dalam masa sama, kerajaan memberi jaminan akan terus memantau perkembangan pasaran minyak dunia dan melakukan penyesuaian harga dari semasa ke semasa. - MYNEWSHUB

Anwar yang juga Menteri Kewangan berkata, harga minyak Malaysia terkesan kerana Selat Hormuz yang merupakan laluan utama minyak dunia terjejas akibat konflik di Timur Tengah.

Bagaimanapun, kata Anwar, demi melindungi rakyat, subsidi kerajaan meningkat daripada sekitar RM700 juta kepada RM3.2 bilion dalam tempoh kurang seminggu

"Rakyat serta majoriti peniaga tidak perlu membayar harga sebenar pasaran kerana subsidi ini disalurkan melalui Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) dan Budi Diesel

"Dalam keadaan dunia yang semakin tidak menentu, usaha melindungi kebajikan dan kesejahteraan rakyat tetap menjadi keutamaan Kerajaan Madani," katanya. - MYNEWSHUB

A question for Dato’, now that you are a PAS member: 

What is PAS’s ultimate political objective in Malaysia?

If PAS’s goal is wholly opposed to Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy and parliamentary system, Malaysians, especially the Malay majority, should know that a PAS takeover would be dangerous and detrimental to Malaysian’s wellbeing!

As YB @rafiziramli noted in his recent Trak Kancil speech, PAS’s present leadership aims to form a theocratic republic like Iran, with a Supreme Leader. What would then happen to our Federal Constitution and constitutional monarchy?

Are theocratic republics such as Iran, Pakistan or Afghanistan more democratic and successful than Malaysia? What does PAS intend to do, if it gains power, about the Federal Constitution and constitutional monarchy?

Replacing or displacing either would be treasonous, and such a party should be banned and outlawed, as Parti Komunis Malaya (PKM) was decades earlier for its communist ideology and for opposing Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy and democratic system.

PAS’s theocratic-republic ideology threatens Malaysians’ rights under the Federal Constitution. Our Raja-raja Melayu should recognise this as treasonous to the sovereignty of the royal institution. Their Majesties must decree to all Malaysians that the Federal Constitution reigns supreme and that the constitutional monarchy must be protected at all costs before PAS gains further ground or a parliamentary majority.

If most Malays ignore the danger and still support PAS, the Federation of Malaysia may crumble if Sabah or Sarawak leaves, as many Malaysians will never accept PAS’s theocratic rule.

A PAS takeover of Putrajaya could also trigger a severe economic crisis: a sharp KLSE crash, unprecedented capital flight and FDI outflow, a collapse of the ringgit (as with Iran’s rial), company closures and relocations, and unemployment at its worst since Merdeka. Industrial unrest could follow as jobs vanish and hardship spreads. Banks could collapse, SMEs fail, shopping malls go bust and bankruptcies multiply. The domino effect would cause a socioeconomic collapse and the worst recession in Malaysia’s history.

Malaysians should learn from Iran’s history and the suffering of Iranians in the decades since the Shah’s fall. Malaysia cannot afford the theocratic state PAS envisions, given its multi-racial, multi-ethnic, multi-religious and multicultural character.

Our founding fathers agreed that a constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy best suit Malaysia. Tunku Abdul Rahman never thought a republic, let alone a theocratic one, was good for the country.

One wonders whether PAS is genuine and trustworthy when its MPs swear allegiance to the Agong, the Raja-raja Melayu and the Constitution, including the ADUNs of the SG4 states, or whether they conceal a more malicious intended outcome once elected in sufficient numbers to take power in Putrajaya.

As a model country with Islam as the official religion under the Federal Constitution, and with the royal monarchy as a sovereign institution, Malaysians should be proud of what Malaysia has achieved since Merdeka without being a theocratic state! 

Politically, socially and economically, Malaysia cannot afford a PAS rule, for the above reasons and the danger its leadership and objectives pose to this nation.

Instead, the main purpose of our political parties and government should be, among others:

1. Eradicate corruption and enforce zero tolerance towards it;

2. Formulate an immediate strategy and action plan to pare down national debt and maintain a sustainable fiscal policy by tightening every ministry’s budget and spending so they are transparent, accountable and measurable;

3. Improve mainstream education so it nurtures and trains our young as STEM professionals to compete locally and globally;

4. Outlaw and prohibit the use of race and religion in politics. Any political party that violates this rule should be banned and deregistered.

3 key messages + 3 key risks from our (World Bank) just released Malaysia economic outlook:

1. Growth upgrade: We upgrade Malaysia’s 2026 growth to 5.1%. This is above regional growth of 4.5%. Malaysia is riding the AI wave

-> Immediate beneficiaries from the data center boom in Malaysia are property developers, construction firms, utility providers. And while higher earnings of these companies means more tax revenues, the extent to which this benefits people-on-the-ground is an open question

2. Moderate inflation: We expect headline inflation this year to be 2% -- among the lowest in the region -- largely due to fuel subsidies. Also, low-income households face milder price pressures. Shows that govt programs such as STR / SARA are helping protect the vulnerable

-> But upstream prices are now on the rise & warrant a close watch: the Producer Price Index went from negative territory just in February to almost 11% in August

3. The current oil price shock is a live test of whether Malaysia’s narrow fiscal space gets rebuilt or eroded further. Higher commodity prices raise revenue but also increase subsidy costs. Subsidies could hit RM40 billion this year (vs RM19 billion in 2025)

-> This highlights the budget’s continued exposure to oil prices, and the importance of not treating higher oil revenues as a permanent source of fiscal space

3 main risks:

1. A reversal in the global AI boom could affect Malaysia’s growth

-> Another risk is the slow rate of AI diffusion in the economy

2. Oil price uncertainty could lead to shortages -- not just of oil -- but also chemicals, fertilizer, food, renewable energy supplies. Food prices in Malaysia can be further affected by a stronger-than-expected El Nino

-> This could be troublesome for Malaysia, where the share of food in the consumer basket is around a high 30%, with a lot of it imported

3. US tariff policy uncertainty continues to weigh on Malaysia’s E&E exports

-> Right now, most E&E exports are exempt from tariffs but that could change
___________
If of interest, happy to elaborate. END/

text:
The mathematics of AFA ~why electricity bills are suddenly hurting

1. Electricity demand is rising fast.
One major new source is data centres.
About 5.7 GW of data-centre supply agreements have already been signed.

For perspective, Peninsular Malaysia’s 2025 peak demand was about 21 GW.
So the potential DC load is huge.

2. When demand rises, TNB has to run more generation.

And lately, more of that extra generation has come from gas.

Gas was around 34–35% of generation previously.
By April 2026, it had risen to around 40%.

More strikingly, gas-fired generation jumped about 50% year-on-year in April, while coal generation fell.

Part of the reason: stronger demand and reduced coal availability.

3. Why does this matter?

Because gas is expensive.

Malaysia is also facing declining domestic gas production.

ST says this means greater dependence on imported LNG.

So when we need more gas generation, we become more exposed to international LNG prices.

4. LNG prices have risen far faster than coal

Over the same broad period, LNG prices rose roughly 3 times more than coal.

And gas was already more expensive per unit of energy than coal.

So the maths is simple:
More gas used × much higher gas price = higher generation cost

5. That higher generation cost flows into AFA.

AFA is designed to adjust electricity bills when fuel and generation costs move away from the base tariff assumptions.

So if gas use rises and LNG becomes more expensive, AFA rises.

6. We have already seen how big the swing can be.

For a household using 1,000 kWh/month:

November 2025
AFA ≈ −8.9 sen/kWh
= about RM89 rebate
August 2026
AFA ≈ +3.8 sen/kWh
= about RM38 extra

Same 1,000 kWh consumption.
Difference:
RM127/month.

7. Government can increase the AFA exemption from 600 kWh to 800 kWh.

That helps in the short term.

But it is still a band-aid.

It does not solve the underlying problem:
higher demand is pushing the system toward more expensive marginal generation.

8. The real reform worth debating is this:

Residential AFA should be based mainly on the lowest-cost generation basket available to the system.

Large new loads, especially data centres and energy-intensive industries, should bear more of the cost of the expensive marginal generation they create.

Why should a household using 1,000 kWh help absorb the extra cost when a new 100 MW data centre forces the grid to run more expensive gas?

That is the real AFA question.

text:
I came across this article about Singapore's new SGD 1 billion support package responding to the Iran war energy shock. Got me curious about how Malaysia's playbook compares.

Let me share what I learnt.

Not better or worse. Just different. And the difference reveals how each country thinks about helping businesses through a crisis.

Singapore's toolkit:

- Direct cash payments (CDC vouchers, COL Special Payment, fuel vouchers for drivers)
- Tax rebates (corporate income tax raised from 40 to 50 percent)
- Grants (EEG expanded to all sectors, Resource Efficiency Grant)
- Targeted subsidies (school bus and disability transport)
- Long-term structural investment (SGD 800 million decarbonisation)
- Government contract fuel cost-sharing mechanism

Malaysia's toolkit:

- Price subsidies (BUDI95 RON95 at RM1.99, diesel subsidy maintained)
- Financing guarantees (RM10 billion SJPP enhanced, RM5 billion BNM SME facility)
- Cash assistance (BUDI Diesel raised from RM200 to RM300 to RM400)
- Regulatory relief (e-invoicing extension to Dec 2027, import duty exemptions)
- Diplomatic intervention (Iran tanker clearance through Strait of Hormuz)
- Internal fiscal adjustments (ministry budget cuts of 10 to 20 percent to fund subsidies)

The structural difference.

Singapore funds support through cash, tax rebates, and grants. Fuel prices reflect global markets. Households and businesses get cash to absorb the shock.

Malaysia funds support through subsidised fuel prices plus financing guarantees plus regulatory relief. Pump prices stay low. The government absorbs the global price differential through its budget.

Both approaches have trade-offs.

Singapore's approach is faster to scale, easier to means-test, and does not distort markets. But Singaporeans see the global oil price every time they fill up.

Malaysia's approach shields most consumers from price volatility entirely. RM1.99 RON95 has not moved despite Brent crude going from US$70 to US$120. But the fiscal cost grows with every escalation.

Which is better I don't know, you decide.

If you optimize for fiscal discipline and market signals, Singapore's playbook is more sustainable.

If you optimize for political stability and protecting low-income households from price shocks, Malaysia's playbook holds prices steady at the cost of fiscal exposure.

The question is what happens if the conflict drags longer. 

Singapore can extend tax rebates and grants because they scale with corporate profit recovery. 

Malaysia's subsidies require continuous fiscal commitment that is already squeezing budget cuts across ministries.

Different playbooks, different break points.

Singapore writes cheques. Malaysia underwrites the price level. Both cost real money. Both reflect different political economies.

Anything I miss out?

🇲🇾According to Reuters on March 24, Asian equities saw US$50.45 billion in net foreign outflows in March, the largest monthly outflow since at least 2008, as investors reacted to oil shock fears and geopolitical tension. The same Reuters report said Brent crude surged as much as 65% this month to US$119.5 per barrel. That tells me the market’s current energy narrative is being driven first by macro stress, not by isolated company stories.
Then, according to Reuters on March 25, the market flipped again. As ceasefire hopes improved, Brent crude fell 5.9% in a single day to US$98.28 per barrel. So this is clearly not a clean, one-direction energy rally. It is a fast-moving, headline-driven market where sentiment can reverse almost overnight.
According to Bernama on March 24, Perdana Petroleum managing director Jamalludin Obeng said sustained higher oil prices could improve the economics of upstream oil and gas projects, which in turn could increase demand for offshore support vessels, offshore logistics, and marine support services. He also said that if instability in West Asia continues, South-East Asia may need to increase production to help support global energy demand. To me, that is one of the clearest signals this week: if the energy theme works in Malaysia, the first beneficiaries may not be every oil and gas counter, but the upstream support and offshore service names tied to actual activity.
At the same time, according to The Star on March 25, citing CGS International Research, every US$10 increase in average oil prices could add around seven basis points to Malaysia’s annual CPI. The same report said prolonged high oil prices could increase fiscal pressure through the RON95 subsidy mechanism, potentially forcing changes in subsidised fuel pricing or the monthly quota structure. In other words, higher oil is not a pure positive for Malaysia. It may help parts of the energy complex, but it also raises inflation and policy risk for the broader market.
There is another important angle here. According to The Star on March 25, MBSB Research maintained a US$90–US$100 Brent assumption and kept a neutral call on Malaysia’s oil and gas sector, while saying that upstream-support players would benefit from a potential pickup in activity if oil prices remain elevated. I think that matters because it reinforces the idea that this is not a “buy everything energy” setup. Even within the sector, the stronger case is selective, not broad-based.
My view: I am interested in Malaysia’s energy space this week, but I am not blindly bullish on the whole board. My bias is toward selected upstream services, offshore support, marine logistics, and energy infrastructure names rather than chasing every stock that happens to move with oil headlines. That is because if crude stays elevated, project economics improve and service demand can be repriced higher. But if ceasefire momentum builds and oil cools further, the first names to lose strength will likely be the ones that only rallied on fear, not on business visibility. This is my inference from how oil, sentiment, and sector research have moved over the past few days.
So my conclusion is straightforward: Malaysia energy is still worth watching this week, but only if you can separate who benefits from oil, who benefits from activity, and who is just moving on emotion. That difference matters more now than ever.

One of my favorite things about making content about different countries is I deep dive into them and learn so many interesting facts.

I am currently researching Malaysia and here is what I have learned: 

- The Malaysian ringgit went from Asia's WORST performing currency 2 years ago to Asia's BEST performing currency. Last year when I came here it was 4.2 ringgit per USD, now it is 3.8

- Singapore and Malaysia have a huge food rivalry and both countries try to claim satay, chicken rice etc 

- 500,000 people commute between Malaysia and Singapore daily. It is one of the busiest border crossings in the world with insane motorcycle traffic and high accident rates

- Singapore gets raw water from Malaysia at 3 cents per 1,000 gallons and sells treated water back at 50 cents per 1,000 gallons. The agreement lasts 100 years. wtf

- Both Trump AND Xi Jinping visited Malaysia in 2025. One of only two countries they both visited last year. 

- Malaysia was one of the first countries to sign a SpaceX satellite contract 

- From 1998 to 2004, the Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world. But what is really interesting is the construction was a competition between a Japan company and a South Korea company. The competition helped make it so they were building one floor every 4 days!

-  Malaysia has a rotating monarchy. Nine sultans take turns being king every 5 years. No other country does this.

- Malaysia has the world's largest cave chamber, the world's largest flower that apparently smells terrible, and are the global leader in rubber glove production

- Malaysia ranked #1 globally in medical tourism. Nomad Capitalist ranked Malaysia as the top medical tourism destination in 2025

-  Grab (Southeast Asia's Uber) was founded by a Malaysian, Anthony Tan, who then moved the HQ to Singapore.

- Malaysia was supposed to be the "Fifth Asian Tiger" in the early 90s. GDP was growing 8% a year. Then the 1997 crisis hit and it never fully recovered

- Malaysia has a bumiputera quota system giving ethnic Malays privileges in university admissions, property, and business

- Borneo's rainforests are 130 million years old. Older than the Amazon.

- Malaysia's current prime minister got put into jail because he was accused of being gay

- The word "ketchup" comes from the Malay/Hokkien word "ke-tsiap"

My take on the current state of the M’sian economy amid geopolitical upheavals [long-ish post]:

But first the global economy. For all the wars, tariffs, general end-of-the-world vibes, the global economy turned out to be…annoyingly resilient, growing about 2.7% last year. This wasn’t economists hallucinating. There were good reasons:

1. Tariffs were louder than they were lethal. Msia's effective tariff rate landed closer to ~12%, not the headline 19%. Same for most countries. Why? Because of carveouts & exemptions.

[As an aside, my colleague @IndermitGill argues that the biggest drag on trade isn’t necessarily tariffs; it’s standards (ie, product safety & environmental rules) that have proliferated like an “invasive species”].

2. Tariffs hit goods, not services trade, which kept humming . In fact, M’sia even clocked its first services trade surplus in 14 years!

3. Emerging markets "showed up". 3 examples:
- Argentina ran a rare budget surplus (yes, Argentina!)
- India grew at 7.4% with low inflation AND low external deficits (no, not a typo!)
- Nigeria’s forex & fuel subsidy reforms delivered its fastest growth in 4 years. In fact, Africa’s growth is now set to outpace Asia’s!

Sure, there are caveats & risks to all the above but the main lesson: Countries that control their steering wheel will steer better.
_______
So, how’s the M’sian economy doing? Pretty good, actually. Inflation is low, growth is solid, real wages are rising... 

...and the ringgit has staged a comeback tour: from a low ~4.7/USD few years ago to 3.9ish/USD these days, making it Asia’s best-performing currency. A strong ringgit is helping bring down prices of imported food items like onions, cabbage, rice. Still, big FX swings, up or down, are not a free lunch. Caution warranted.

Tourism has been a surprise bright spot. But caution warranted: Malaysia should avoid playing the visitor numbers / volume game. The smarter move is to maximize value per visitor, for ex, through experience-led tourism a la New Zealand, Costa Rica, Kenya. (Mulu caves, anyone?)

Now, one angst area is AI & jobs: About half of Malaysian workers face high automation risk. About a quarter are exposed to generative AI. 

Job losses are real but history shows how broad tech waves create new jobs, much like the internet era of the 1990s. Back then, nobody could have predicted that the most desirable jobs would be in the likes of FB, Apple, Google etc. Indeed, early AI-era roles are already emerging: AI trainers, data curators, prompt engineers. And “human-touch” jobs, like elder care, could see huge, rising returns. For an ageing M’sia, this is a wide-open, underexplored opportunity.

So AI AIn’t going away. The real Q is how we prepare the next gen. Merely introducing tech / gadgets into classrooms in attempt to “modernize education” isn’t the answer. Foundations matter much more: building literacy, numeracy, collaboration, socio-emotional skills. We can also be inspired by Nobelists Banerjee & Duflo who provide a simple 2 step approach to improve learning outcomes:
Step 1: Figure out what kids actually know (shockingly hard).
Step 2: Help them get there (AI could make this easier via personalized learning).
Which also means schools should teach the kids they have, not the ones they wish they had.
_______
Ok, this is starting to sound like a Substack post so I’ll stop here…but there's plenty more to say on M'sia:
- New findings on the business environment
- Oddly overlooked issue of long-term joblessness
- Why preventive health is so hard (hint: it’s not always supply but, surprisingly, lack of demand).

Maybe I’ll cover these in future posts, but for this one, the bottom line is that Msia’s hands are on the steering wheel for now... 

...and the payoff of managing geopolitics will matter most if they continue to show up in everyday life: lower cost of living, better jobs, kids with strong foundations to help them navigate an uncertain future. 

Everything else is, well, just…commentary. END/

Speech at Parti Putra  HQ
What new  do we  need in a new Malay PM?

At independence, an all-Malay political party served an explicit and legitimate purpose. Malays were economically weak, politically fragmented, and vulnerable in a colonial system that had favoured others. Unity was necessary for survival.

But that historical moment has passed.

Islam is constitutionally entrenched as the religion of the Federation.
The Malay Rulers are secure. To be respected, they may need to do more themselves. 
Bahasa Melayu is firmly established as the national language.
Article 153 has long been implemented, arguably beyond its original intent, through dominance in the civil service, preferential licensing, university access, and control of government-linked companies.

So the question must be asked honestly: what is left for the Malays to strive for

The answer is the economy. Malays have little of the real economy other than the formal institutions  

Malays have yet to “catch up” in business, particularly in comparison with the Chinese business community. Some go further and say that until this changes, Malays will always remain employees rather than owners. We need a Prime Minister who understands this

Economic dominance is not dismantled through protection. It is dismantled through competition and by government intervention. meaningful Malay participation in business means Malaysia needs a new economic model. The new PM must understand this 

We need a semi-socialist government of Xi Jin Prng and Vladimir Putin. With Malaysian characteristics of course 
Those countries are world class success stories we must emulate; and we must ask them how it's done.

We have to remove leaders who prefer
to dance with Trump and follow the economic model set by Wall Street that enriches two per cent of the population

Business success does not come from quotas, licences, or political patronage. Or grocery stores subsidies. It comes from skill, discipline, risk-taking, long hours, innovation, failure, and persistence. These are not racial traits. They are habits formed by systems that reward merit and punish incompetence. A progressive Malay  government has to be formed to
Implement them. Isn't that what  Maufakat Nasional is for

Yet our politics continues to do the opposite.

Protection has produced rent-seekers instead of entrepreneurs. Guaranteed access has removed the need to compete. Government-linked comfort has benefited top civil servants and political operators who have no love for the country.

Worst of all, religion has been misused as an excuse for self-limitation.

If Vincent Tan and Genting can do billion Ringgit business why can't similar licences be issued to the Malays? If the government leaders tell you that you are not to do business that are “ sinful” that's their excuse to continue to give such monopolies to the non Malays for which they are well rewarded

Remember when the social welfare lottery benefited millions of the poor but was scrapped. And privatised to a few. Why do we enrich them to our detriment? 

Malays must have the same rights  for business opportunities as the others. There is now more than 60 billion worth of business that Malays are precluded from participating as they are considered sinful activities.  

If we can find ways to to accommodate riba which is haram and Islamic methods of mudhrabah and Sukuk; why can't we find ways to legitimse other commercial activitues. What are the scholars doing?

As long as Malays rely on ethnic politics and for shelter, they will never out-compete those who learned to survive without it.

Even in the political arena Malays are weak and lethargic. Look at Perlis. Are they fighting for the people? Perlis  remain poor

You cannot demand respect if you are afraid of the challenges. You can't get permanent protection and expect world-class performance. No community in history has become strong by being timid to protect their  rights.

text:
Big Oil slashes jobs and investments as low crude prices bite | Malcolm Moore & Jamie Smyth, Financial Times

Lay-offs mark ‘flashing red warning light’ for industry as executives brace for downturn that may last years

The world’s biggest oil and gas companies are cutting jobs, slashing costs and scaling back investments at the fastest pace since the coronavirus market collapse, as executives brace for a prolonged period of lower crude prices.

Thousands of jobs have been cut across the industry at companies including Chevron and BP, with tens of billions of additional cost savings promised. Spending plans have been reined in, with some projects paused or put up for sale as groups seek to balance the books.

The US shale industry has been hit particularly hard, with ConocoPhillips last week becoming the latest to axe staff in response to the downturn.

“This isn’t just a Conoco problem,” Kirk Edwards, head of Latigo Petroleum, an independent producer in Texas, said of the job losses. “It’s a flashing red warning light for the entire US oil and gas industry.”

Even the largest state-run energy companies have not been immune, with Saudi Aramco selling a $10bn stake in a pipeline network to raise cash and Petronas of Malaysia cutting 5,000 jobs from its workforce.

Crude prices have halved from the peak that followed Russia’s full invasion of Ukraine in 2022, while an Opec+ decision at the weekend to continue boosting output, despite forecasts of a looming supply glut, will add to the price pressure.

The cartel has over the past five months pivoted from a strategy of restraining production and propping up prices to winning back market share and crushing higher-cost rivals in the US and other non-Opec nations.

Wood Mackenzie has forecast benchmark Brent crude would fall below $60 a barrel in early 2026 and remain there for “up to a few years” — barring a geopolitical shock. Brent traded at just under $66 on Monday.

At less than $60 none of the big western oil companies can cover their investment plans and the dividends and buybacks that investors expect. Morgan Stanley expects them to cut their buybacks in the months ahead, while BP has already done so.

Borrowing levels, meanwhile, have crept back up to the levels last seen before the 2022 oil boom that allowed producers to pay down their debt.

Capital spending on global oil and gas production is forecast to drop 4.3 per cent this year to $341.9bn, the first annual fall in investment since 2020, according to Wood Mackenzie.

The US Energy Information Administration last month said the slowdown in capital investment in the US would cause production in the world’s biggest oil-producing nation to fall for the first time since 2021.

The human consequences are stark in Texas, centre of the US industry and location of the giant oil-producing Permian Basin. ConocoPhillips chief executive Ryan Lance told employees that as many as one in four of them, or up to 3,250 people, would be out of work by Christmas. Chevron’s cuts of up to 8,000 jobs have been under way since February.

Both companies have been pushing through sweeping restructurings following big acquisitions, with management consultancies hired to oversee the reductions.

“The way we protect the most jobs for the most people is by remaining competitive,” Chevron chief executive Mike Wirth said last month. “We have to take control of our own future.”

In the UK, BP in January said it was cutting 4,700 jobs in an effort to improve shareholder returns.

ExxonMobil is best placed among the oil majors, analysts say, owing to its low debt and free cash flows that exceeded $14bn in the first half of 2025.

Big oil companies are also leaning on outsourcing and new technologies, with administrative, accounting and skilled engineering jobs moving to countries such as India and artificial intelligence offering opportunities to do more with less.

Anwar Takes the Heat: Why His Cuts Could Secure Malaysia’s Tomorrow...!!
@anwaribrahim 
While many politicians win support by loosening purse strings, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has charted a different course — one that’s drawn significant backlash.

With soaring prices, the end of diesel subsidies, an expanded SST, and the average Malaysian feeling the squeeze, tensions are high. Yet, beneath the surface, Anwar’s efforts are not about deepening the crisis but curbing a financial hemorrhage.

Facing Malaysia’s Fiscal Reality
For decades, Malaysia has outspent its income, a predicament called a budget deficit. Imagine earning RM3,000 monthly yet spending RM4,000. Borrowing can tide you over temporarily, but the debt pile grows, and the burden falls on us — and our children.

Inheriting a legacy of reckless expenditure, Anwar opted to confront it directly, unlike his predecessors who kicked the can down the road. The deficit stood at 5% of GDP in 2023, fell to 4.1% by 2024, and continues to decline in 2025’s first quarter.

Targeted Reforms, Tangible Savings
His most controversial move — scrapping blanket diesel subsidies — saved over RM20 billion (exceeding USD 4 billion). Rather than subsidizing fuel for all, including the affluent and foreigners, support now reaches those who truly need it. It’s a calculated, logical step, though deeply unpopular.

And the results are emerging.

A Stand Against Global Trends
Compare this to the U.S. under Donald Trump, where deficit reduction promises gave way to a ballooning national debt fueled by tax cuts and populist spending. Even affluent nations struggle with deficits, yet Malaysia, a small developing country, is quietly succeeding where giants falter — living within its means for future generations.

Short-Term Pain, Long-Term Promise
The economic pressure Malaysians feel today is real but necessary. Securing our finances could strengthen the ringgit, ease import inflation, enhance schools, hospitals, and infrastructure, and most importantly, reduce the debt passed to our kids.

Ignore the deficit, and the future looms grim: rising taxes, a weaker currency, job losses, and risks of collapse akin to Sri Lanka, Venezuela, or Greece. Is that the legacy we envision?

A Moral Stand, A Shared Responsibility
Anwar’s approach lacks political expediency — it may jeopardize his next election. Yet, it’s a courageous moral choice, aiming to fortify Malaysia for tomorrow. The harsh truth: a loss could see a new government reverse course, erasing this progress with reckless spending.

We must decide: do we want leaders who prioritize popularity with empty promises, or those who embrace the hard road for justice?

And what of Malaysia’s states? Some flounder in debt from overhyped mega-projects with little return. Are chief ministers cutting personal extravagances, freezing unnecessary costs, or auditing bloated agencies? If Anwar faces national backlash to save the nation, why aren’t state governments following suit?

A Moment for Collective Vision
Malaysians must see this moment clearly. Your wallet may feel lighter now, but parents, your child will thank you someday. Youth, your future — taxes, living costs, job security — depends on today’s actions.

The perspective shifts from “Why is Anwar leading this charge?” to a pressing wonder: “Why was this overdue?”

This year, there’s little room left for such maneuvers

My prediction of a highly pressured Madani budget is coming true.

text:
Dear bro Eric,
I get why you highlight "Madani borrows RM69B while Najib only RM32B". But let’s be fair - raw numbers without full context mislead more than they inform.
Najib’s era had oil at USD54/barrel avg in 2017- GDP growth strong, global rates low - plus hidden debts via 1MDB & off-book guarantees. COVID then forced RM115B extra debt 2020–22. End-2017 direct debt was RM686.8B- today it’s RM1.31T - yes, up RM623B, but pandemic & weak ringgit alone add hundreds of billions.

Madani’s spending also props up fuel, electricity & rice subsidies so Rakyat don’t face overnight tariff shock. Remove subsidies? Prices spike - Rakyat still pay.

The real issue isn’t just "who borrows more", but-
1- Are we borrowing for productive growth?
2- Are we plugging leakages?
3- Or just rolling debt for politics?

Najib’s lower borrowings rode on oil money. Madani inherited COVID hangover, sluggish economy, weak ringgit, plus record subsidy bills. Debt servicing is now Malaysia’s 2nd biggest expense - so fiscal reform must widen the tax base & cut wastage, not just make the Rakyat "help" blindly.
Let’s be fair- cherry-picking numbers spins half the truth, but pretending Najib’s era was "prudent" while Madani’s is reckless is half-baked. Tell the full story- honest books matter more than slogans. Debt isn’t free. We pay either way - the question is, does it build Malaysia up, or leak Malaysia dry!

The Increase Of Electricity Tariff

They promised Malaysians that the MADANI Government would keep the cost of living under control.

Now look at the electricity tariff.

The domestic base tariff increased from 39.95 sen to 45.40 sen/kWh — a 13.64% increase.

This is what “keeping electricity affordable” looks like?

Raise the tariff, dress it up with a complicated pricing structure, then tell Malaysians that they should feel relieved because most households may not see an increase in their final bill.

At the same time, TNB is a monopoly and continues to report strong annual profits. For the financial year ended 31 December 2023, TNB recorded a profit after tax of approximately RM2.77 billion.

What about 2025?

If TNB continues to make billions in profit, Malaysians have every right to ask:

Why should ordinary households pay more for electricity while TNB remains profitable?

Is this tariff increase genuinely necessary, or are Malaysians being asked to shoulder higher costs to protect TNB’s profitability?

Malaysians don’t live on government press statements.

They live on salaries, grocery bills, petrol bills and electricity bills.

If this is MADANI’s idea of keeping costs low, Malaysians have every right to ask:

How much more must ordinary Malaysians pay before the promises finally mean something?  

@anwaribrahim @MOFmalaysia @Tenaga_Nasional

text:
2/2

The 6 sen sweetener was not an oversight. It was a deliberate political instrument to make the reform palatable — ensuring ordinary Malaysians paid less at the pump on launch day, generating goodwill while simultaneously neutralising the fiscal dividend. Nobody in the financial press netted it off. Nobody in parliament questioned it. The bond market never saw it.

A Reform Designed Not to Reform

The deeper indictment of Budi95 is philosophical, not arithmetic. A subsidy genuinely designed to reduce wasteful fuel consumption would function as a declining block tariff — protecting the first 80 litres fully, introducing price signals at the margin, and penalising excessive consumption progressively. Malaysia already uses this model for electricity. It works.

Instead, Budi95 maintains a flat RM1.99 price across all consumption up to 300 litres — the most effective possible design for maximising consumption, not reducing it. Thirty years of artificially cheap fuel have given Malaysia car-dependent urban sprawl, a fuel-inefficient national vehicle fleet, chronically underused public transport, and transport emissions incompatible with every net-zero commitment the government has signed. Budi95 entrenches every one of these distortions for another generation.

The real annual cost of these behavioural distortions — excess congestion, suppressed public transport, suboptimal urban form, carbon externalities — conservatively exceeds RM20-50 billion. Against this, arguing about whether the cap should be 140 or 300 litres is rearranging deck chairs.

Why Nobody Said So

The RM8 billion fiction survived unchallenged for a simple reason: everyone had an incentive to believe it. The government needed reform credibility. Bond investors needed a narrative to justify buying Malaysian debt. Rating agencies needed a checkbox. The opposition did not want to be seen defending fuel subsidies for the rich. Civil society was relieved the poor kept their RM1.99.

The numbers were always public. The MoF distribution chart, the pre-reform pump price, the Month 1 consumption data — all published, all accessible. The arithmetic required nothing more than a calculator and thirty minutes.

Malaysia's financial journalism failed its most basic function: to hold a number to account.

The Verdict

Budi95 was not a fiscal reform. It was a fiscal communication exercise — expertly executed, politically astute, and arithmetically empty. The ringgit rally it helped trigger was built partly on a foundation of RM140 million in real savings dressed up as RM8 billion. Markets priced in a transformation that delivered a rounding error.

The myth of Budi95 will eventually meet its reckoning — at the next oil price spike, the next ringgit depreciation, or the next budget where the subsidy line refuses to shrink. When that moment arrives, the question will not be why the government inflated the numbers. The question will be why nobody checked.
