The growing calls for solidarity with Palestine is a testament to Malaysia's commitment to justice. But in two days, as ASEAN Summit hosts, we have a rare chance to turn passion into progress. Protests are vital, but disrupting Trump's visit risks closing the door on the very conversations that can shift U.S. policy.

Imagine PM Anwar, backed by ASEAN, at the table with Trump. He has a unique opening to appeal to Trump's legacy. He can argue that Israel's constant ceasefire violations are a direct insult to the Gaza peace deal Trump brokered. This is our chance to persuade him to protect his own deal with a firmer stance and remind him of his promise to ensure that the West Bank is not annexed by Israel.

This leverage opens the door for real steps: aid corridors, UN resolutions, and rallying other leaders. Quiet diplomacy has worked for us before. Alienating Trump now only helps hardliners and dooms any hope of swaying the West.

Pragmatically, ASEAN's $100B+ in U.S. exports are at stake. Trump's tariff threats could crush our SMEs. By welcoming him with firm resolve, not fists, we secure a platform to negotiate. Here in Asia, we understand this: even rival gangsters sit down for a 'table talk' to solve issues. It’s about protecting our interests and our people.

This isn't capitulation; it's strategy. As Malaysians, we should instead channel our fire into advocacy that lands results. We should take advantage and embrace this moment for the sake of Palestine and our economy. Turn outrage into outcomes.
#ASEAN2025 #DiplomacyWins #FreePalestineThroughEngagement

Palestinian liberation advocacy group Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) Malaysia today announced that it will hold a joint protest with more than 23 partner organisations on Oct 26, to express their opposition to US President Donald Trump’s presence at the Asean Summit in Kuala Lumpur.

Group chairperson Nazari Ismail said that although they respected the government’s official stance and diplomatic approaches, the public should still be allowed to express their views through a peaceful gathering in solidarity with the people of Palestine.

“We hope that millions of Malaysians will come out to show their displeasure and disagreement with the policies of the American government, now headed by Trump.

“Although we respect Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s decision as a country, we personally believe that Trump is still not welcome,” Nazari said at a press conference in Kuala Lumpur today.

text:
Trumpism 2.0 is showing up the bankruptcy of Madani
Murray Hunter
Nov 19

Since Donald Trump won the US presidency for a second time around, no time has been wasted in selecting a group of change agents to transform US administration. Trump was elected with a well publicized agenda, which included securing US national borders which have caused many social issues with the inflow of illegal immigrants across the country, and fighting the increasing cost of living.

Trump has picked up on this mandate and selected very capable people. This process of going on with new announcements being made on a daily basis.

Trump after two assassination attempts is not hiding from the public, much to the concern of those near him. Trump is receiving heroic welcomes wherever he goes, something akin to a superstar.

Interestingly Trump is putting a major focus on trimming the size and wastage going on in government. The forthcoming Department of Government Efficiency, DOGE as Elon Musk likes to call it, aims to trim billions off the US government budget.

The plight of education in the US is not being ignored either. The Federal Department of Education will be disbanded and rebuilt from the ground.

There is a great realization that high quality education is needed to ‘Make America Great Again”.

Trump is also focused on destroying the censorship that the government-media-Big Tech deep state has created. Free speech is being revitalised. Trumpism believes there can be no democracy without free speech.

Trump is poised to be at the cutting edge of reform. This makes for a very exciting time in the US over the next four years.

Excitement verses bankruptcy

In November 2022, Anwar Ibrahim generated much excitement after his 24 year quest to become prime minister.

There was an expectation that Anwar would reform the Sedition Act, and bring true freedom of speech to Malaysia. There were also high hopes that Anwar would improve Malaysia’s economic circumstances, so the average family would be better off and be able to afford to live. Most of all, people hoped that Anwar would create a true sense of multiculturalism in Malaysia.

Two years into the Anwar administration, so many traditional supporters are disappointed. Even voters within the Malay heartlands have not warmed to Anwar.

Anwar is propped up by an agreement between the old elites, after a hung parliament. He is disappointing those who put him there for failing to live up to his side of the bargain.

Malaysia has less freedom of speech than ever before. Malaysia is more racially divided than ever before. A democracy is being turned into an Islamic Caliph, through a backdoor circumventing of the constitution.

Anwar’s economic plans are great for the elites. Anwar is reinforcing feudalism post haste. Those who point out these facts are persecuted with the draconian laws his party promised to abolish.

The sadist thing about the Madani regime is it is bankrupt of any new ideas. Even the minister of economy had to call in Toh Pah for help, and those who lost their seats in the general election have been given senior positions in the government. Meritocracy has been caste aside with political appointees, and the legal system is being weaponised and lenient for their friends. DNAAs and discounts on sentences are rewards for the elite.

Malaysians, particularly the traditional supporters of Anwar have been following US politics, especially the presidential race. The US election has been a fairytale to them, a story of what could be. They get excited about the hope Trump is giving people, only to wake up with a nightmare that exists in Malaysia today under Madani.

For Malaysia Trump has shown what could be here in Malaysia.

Of late, Malaysia has been perceived as tilting to one side, in a so- called strategic pivot from another side. This is not only an oversimplification, but in fact, is a gross misperception of our national interests and character.

The truth is Malaysia will always be on the side of Malaysia! We are fiercely independent. We refuse to be defined by how major powers see the world. 

So we will continue to strive for our national and strategic interests, defined on our own terms.

Malaysia maintains a strong and fruitful relationship with both China and the United States. In fact, we mark milestones with both countries this year. Ten years ago, Malaysia and the US upgraded our bilateral relationship into a Strategic Partnership. 

I frequently reiterate the importance of US-based foreign direct investment to Malaysia. The US is our largest investor in fact, especially in high-tech sectors.

This year too, Malaysia celebrates the 50th anniversary of ties with China – now our largest trade partner, a key investor and a close bilateral and multilateral partner.

There are however, situations that call for unhesitating and unequivocal intervention. The Israeli occupation of Palestine is a scourge on our collective histories and the conduct of nations.

Malaysia is no major power, but we are sovereign and free. And make no mistake, we will use our freedom to support the Palestinians’ fight for theirs. We have consistently voiced concerns about the reluctance of the US and the West to apply pressure on Israel.

President Biden has recently begun to push for acceptance of a proposal for a ceasefire in exchange for the release of hostages. We welcome these early signs of change in America's approach and hope the US will use its leverage to end the killings and carnage.

Our neutrality and our advocacy for among the world’s most oppressed peoples, go hand in hand. It also represents, we believe, the feelings of millions of Malaysians.

#MalaysiaMADANI

MALAYSIANS AND HUMAN TRAGEDY
 
1. It is sad to see that in Malaysia, there are people who think that the Israeli attack against Gaza is a matter of concern only to the Muslims. It should not be so regarded. It is not even a war between the Israelis and the Palestinians. It is a case of criminal oppression of a powerful people against a weak people. It is in fact an international crime.
 
2. We abhor bullying in school. But in this case the bullying is done by a strong country against a weak people. It involves killing men, women, children and babies. Our condemnation of this bullying should be stronger. But obviously some of us don’t. We think it is the problem of Muslims. Non-Muslims should not care.
 
3. But in civilised human societies laws do not differentiate between race or religion. Laws apply to everyone equally. Thus if you murder someone, you have committed a crime whether you are of any race or religion.
 
4. What we are seeing in Palestine is not a war between two countries. What we are seeing is an attempt by the Israelis to commit genocide on the Palestinian. Genocide is a crime. If it had been genocide by the Palestinians against the Israelis, it would still be a crime.
 
5. So we should all object to this. Whether we are Muslims or Christians or even if we are of the same religion as the Jews we should protest against the barbaric acts that are being perpetrated now in Gaza and the West Bank.
 
6. So I hope that Malaysians of whatever origin, whether they be Muslims or non Muslims, Christians or Buddhists or Hindus should not consider this as something that is happening only to Muslims. It this happening to fellow human beings. Remember millions of Muslims died to defeat Germany and to end the oppression of the Jews.
 
7. We claim that we are all Malaysians. Yet we are showing the division between us over this human tragedy.

DR MAHATHIR BIN MOHAMAD
Dec 5, 2023
